ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two identical light springs have a stiffness coefficient of $k = 100 \, \mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$. They are used to suspend a uniform horizontal metal rod PQ of length $L = 2 \, \mathrm{m}$ and mass $m = 0.1 \, \mathrm{kg}$ at rest. The metal rod is placed in a uniform magnetic field directed horizontally outward. When a current $I = 3 \, \mathrm{A}$ flows from end P to end Q in the metal rod, each spring elongates by $x = 2 \, \mathrm{cm}$. The acceleration due to gravity is $g = 10 \, \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The magnitude and direction of the Ampere force acting on the metal rod.
2. The magnitude of the magnetic induction of this uniform magnetic field.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Two identical light springs have a stiffness coefficient of $k = 100\,\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$. They are used to suspend a uniform horizontal metal rod PQ of length $L = 2\,\mathrm{m}$ and mass $m = 0.1\,\mathrm{kg}$ at rest. The metal rod is placed in a uniform magnetic field directed horizontally outward. When a current $I = 3\,\mathrm{A}$ flows from end P to end Q in the metal rod, each spring elongates by $x = 2\,\mathrm{cm}$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the metal rod PQ is placed horizontally, P is at the left end, and Q is at the right end; near the two ends of the rod, each is suspended by a vertical spring, and the springs connect upward to the fixed support above. There are many dot symbols in the figure and it is marked B, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper outward; the current arrow on the metal rod is from left to right, namely from P to Q. Reasoning: Both springs provide upward elastic force to the rod. The current direction is to the right, and the magnetic field direction is perpendicular to the plane of the paper outward. According to the left-hand rule or the vector relation F = I L × B, the direction of the Ampere force is vertically downward. After being energized, each spring elongates x = 2 cm = 0.02 m, therefore the total upward elastic force of the two springs is 2kx = 2 × 100 × 0.02 = 4 N. The rod's gravity is mg = 0.1 × 10 = 1 N, directed downward. The rod is at rest, and the forces in the vertical direction are balanced, so 2kx = mg + F_A, obtaining F_A = 4 - 1 = 3 N, directed vertically downward. Since the rod is perpendicular to the magnetic field, the magnitude of the Ampere force F_A = BIL, therefore B = F_A/(IL) = 3/(3 × 2) = 0.5 T.
